relatedSnapshot.title: Tidy up CRM template settings and copy names after personal templates
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Follow-up to ENG-13830. Personal and team templates shipped with a few rough edges and some duplicated code that reviewers agreed can wait. Fixing them keeps the email and SMS template screens consistent and makes the next change to them cheaper.

## What's included

* **Make personal copy with long names:** "Make personal copy" appends " (copy)". A team template whose name is 194 to 200 characters then goes over the name limit, and a name clash has no rename path. Generate a copy name that fits, and let the person rename it when it clashes.
* **Capability check failures:** if the check for whether personal templates are available fails, Save as template and New template are blocked behind a retry banner. Consider defaulting to Team and hiding the checkbox instead, while still sending visibility explicitly from the client.
* **Fewer database round trips:** the template access check reads the member table twice per list, get and mark-used call. Fetch the role once.
* **Shared pieces:** the visibility badge, the Share with team checkbox, the capability banner and the duplicate-name rule are copied across both settings pages, both save dialogs and both pickers. Move them into small shared components and a helper. Combine the page's editing state into one object.
* **Schema and router duplication:** move the shared bulk-delete transform and visibility schema into one module. Add a note on the rolling-deploy input shapes saying when they can be removed. Consider one template service shared by the email and SMS routers.

## Done when

- [ ] A personal copy of any valid team template can be created, and a name clash offers a rename.
- [ ] The duplicated UI pieces and schemas live in one place each, with no change in behaviour, and the existing template tests pass.

relatedSnapshot.title: Create and manage SMS templates in settings
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Give people a place in settings to write and look after their workspace's text-message templates, the same way they already look after email templates.

## Problem

Once saved templates exist there is still no way for a person to create one. Without a management screen, every template a rep might insert would have to be created by an engineer.

## Proposed fix

Add an SMS Templates page to the same settings area that already holds Email Templates. It lists the workspace's templates, lets a person search them, write a new one, rename or edit an existing one, and delete one or several at a time. A template is a name and a plain-text message, with no subject and no formatting, because that is all a text can carry.

## What's included

* An SMS Templates destination in settings, reachable from the settings menu and the command palette.
* A list showing each template's name, the start of its message, who created it and when it last changed.
* Search across name and message.
* Write, rename and edit through one form with a name and a plain-text message.
* Delete one template, with confirmation.
* Select several and delete them together, with confirmation.
* Loading, empty, no-results, error and permission-denied states.

Not included: the composer picker, placeholder handling, importing or exporting, folders, categories, and duplicating a template.

## Blocked by

* Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace

## How it should work

* The page shows only the current workspace's templates.
* A name already in use is refused with a clear message, and the person keeps everything they typed.
* The message box is plain text with no formatting controls, and shows how much of the available length is used.
* A person who is not allowed to change a template is not offered rename, edit or delete, and the attempt is refused if it is made anyway.
* Deleting asks for confirmation and names what is going. Deleting several says how many.
* A template that has already been used still deletes. Texts already sent are unaffected, because a sent text keeps its own copy of the message.
* If the list cannot load, the page says so and offers to try again rather than showing an empty library.

## Who can do what

Anyone in the workspace can open the page, search and read, and anyone in the workspace can write a new template. Renaming, editing and deleting are limited to whoever created the template, plus workspace owners and admins. The page appears for workspaces that have texting.

## What the user sees

An SMS Templates entry in the settings menu and in the command palette. The page lists templates with a search box and a button to write a new one. Writing or editing opens a form with a name and a message. An empty library invites them to write the first one. A search with no matches says so and offers to clear it. A failure to load says so and offers to retry. Actions a person is not allowed to take are not shown.

## Done when

- [ ] The page is reachable from the settings menu and from the command palette.
- [ ] A person can write, rename, edit and delete a template and see the list update.
- [ ] Several templates can be selected and deleted together after confirming.
- [ ] Search narrows the list by name and by message.
- [ ] A duplicate name is refused clearly and nothing typed is lost.
- [ ] Someone who did not create a template is not offered rename, edit or delete.
- [ ] Empty, no-results, loading, error and permission-denied states all render.
- [ ] Only the current workspace's templates appear.
- [ ] The page appears for a workspace with texting and not for one without it.
- [ ] Browser QA covers writing, editing, deleting, bulk deleting and every state above.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A workspace can build and look after its own library of text-message templates without engineering help, ready for the composer picker to read.

## Implementation context

* Follow the existing Email Templates settings page, minus the subject field and the rich-text editor. A text has no subject and carries no formatting, so the message box is plain and the page is smaller than its email counterpart.
* This page belongs behind the feature that gates texting, not the one that gates cold email. Copying the email page's gate exactly would hide the page from a workspace that has phones but not cold email, and show it to one that has neither.
* Wider background for this work is in the AI context.md on the parent ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Give CRM somewhere to keep a reusable text message. This ticket adds the saved template itself and the rules for reading and writing one, so the later settings screen and the composer picker both have a single place to work from.

## Problem

CRM has reusable email templates but nothing equivalent for texts. There is no record of a saved text message anywhere, so no screen can list one and no composer can insert one.

## Proposed fix

Add a saved SMS template that belongs to a workspace, carries a name and a plain-text message, and can be listed, searched, created, renamed, edited and deleted under the same rules email templates already follow. Also record when each person last used each template, so the picker built later can offer their recent ones first.

Nothing user-visible ships in this ticket. It is the foundation the other two build on.

## What's included

* A saved SMS template with a name and a plain-text message.
* A record of when each person last used each template.
* List with search, read one, create, rename, edit, delete, delete several at once, and mark used.
* Workspace scoping on every read and write.
* Names unique within a workspace, ignoring letter case.
* Message length capped to what a text can actually carry.
* Deletion that keeps the record rather than destroying it.
* One shared way for the screens built later to read and change templates, so neither of them has to depend on the other.
* Preview environments seeded with this data.

Not included: any screen, the composer picker, placeholder handling, sharing beyond the existing email-template rules, folders or categories, and default seeded templates.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* A template belongs to one workspace and is visible to everyone in it.
* A name already used in that workspace is refused, and a difference in letter case is not a way around it.
* The message is capped at the same length the existing texting routes enforce, so a template can never hold a message that cannot be sent.
* Deleting marks the template deleted and records who did it. Deleted templates disappear from every list and cannot be read, renamed or deleted again.
* Deleting several at once refuses the whole request if any one of them is missing or not that person's to delete, rather than partly succeeding.
* Marking a template used records the moment for that person only, and repeating it updates the existing record rather than adding another.
* A request naming a template in another workspace is refused and changes nothing.

## Who can do what

Anyone in the workspace who can send a text can list, read, create one, and record that they used one. Renaming, editing and deleting are limited to whoever created the template, plus workspace owners and admins. Nobody can reach a template in another workspace.

These are the rules email templates follow, with one deliberate difference: recording a use is treated as a write here rather than as a read. A client role cannot send a text at all, so recording that it used a template would be a write with nothing behind it. Email has no equivalent restriction because its send route does not have one.

## What the user sees

Not applicable: this ticket ships no user-visible surface. Its behavior becomes visible through the settings screen and the composer picker that follow it.

## Done when

- [ ] A template can be created, listed, searched, read, renamed, edited and deleted.
- [ ] Two templates in the same workspace cannot share a name, including when only letter case differs.
- [ ] A message longer than a text can carry is refused.
- [ ] A deleted template is absent from every read and cannot be changed again.
- [ ] Deleting several at once either does all of them or none.
- [ ] Someone from another workspace is refused and nothing is written.
- [ ] Only the creator, an owner or an admin can rename, edit or delete.
- [ ] Marking used keeps one record per person per template and updates it on repeat.
- [ ] Preview environments contain this data without leaving broken references.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A saved SMS template exists as real, workspace-scoped, permission-checked data, so the settings screen and the composer picker can each be built without inventing storage of their own.

## Implementation context

* Mirror the completed email template implementation rather than designing a second template system. It already settles naming rules, soft deletion, the recent-use record and the permission split.
* The message cap must match the limit the existing send and schedule routes enforce, not the far larger email body limit, so a template can never be saved that those routes would then refuse.
* A new table needs both its preview-dump entry and orphan cleanup for any foreign key pointing into a table that is only partly copied. Nothing in CI catches that omission.
* Wider background for this work is in the AI context.md on the parent ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Insert a saved SMS template into the contact text composer
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let a rep pick a saved template while writing a text on a contact record, so a common message does not have to be retyped, and can still be edited before it goes.

## Problem

A rep sending the same text over and over has to retype it every time. Even once templates exist and can be managed, there is no way to get one into the box where a text is actually written.

## Proposed fix

Put a template picker beside the message box on the contact's Calls and Texts tab. It searches the workspace's templates, offers the ones that rep used most recently first, and fills the message box with the one they choose. The message stays fully editable and works with both Send now and Send later. Choosing a template never sends or schedules anything by itself.

## What's included

* A searchable template picker beside the message box on the contact record.
* Recently used templates offered first, per rep.
* Choosing a template fills the message box and leaves it editable.
* Confirmation before replacing a message that has already been typed.
* Works with Send now and with Send later.
* A warning before sending when the message still contains placeholders that will not be filled in.
* Loading, empty, no-results and error states in the picker.
* The picker hidden where texting is unavailable, on sample contacts, and where the contact has asked to stop receiving texts.
* Activation tracking for choosing and using a template.

Not included: saving the current message as a new template, managing templates from the composer, filling placeholders in automatically, and any change to how a text is sent or scheduled.

## Blocked by

* Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace

## How it should work

* Choosing a template puts its message in the box and nothing else happens. Nothing is sent and nothing is scheduled.
* If the box already has something in it, the rep is asked to confirm before it is replaced, and can cancel and keep what they wrote.
* If the box is empty the template goes straight in without asking.
* Name 1 a template is recorded for that rep, so it appears under recent next time.
* A message containing placeholders that will not be filled in raises the same warning email already raises, and the rep can send anyway or go back and edit. Placeholders are never substituted, because they are not substituted for email either.
* Send now and Send later both act on whatever is in the box at that moment, whether it came from a template or was typed by hand.
* Where texting is unavailable the picker is not offered at all, rather than offered and then failing.

## Who can do what

Any rep who can send a text from the contact record can search and insert any template in their workspace. Inserting does not create, change or delete a template. Writing and looking after templates stays in settings.

## What the user sees

A template control beside the message box. Opening it shows a search box, that rep's recently used templates, then the rest, each with its name and the start of its message. Searching narrows the list, and no matches says so. An empty library points them at settings. A failure to load says so. Choosing one fills the box. Replacing text already typed asks first. Placeholders left in the message raise a warning at the moment of sending.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep can search for and insert a template from the contact Calls and Texts composer.
- [ ] The inserted message can be edited before it goes.
- [ ] An inserted template can be sent now.
- [ ] An inserted template can be scheduled for later.
- [ ] Replacing a message already typed asks for confirmation and can be cancelled.
- [ ] Inserting into an empty box does not ask.
- [ ] A template used once appears under recent for that rep next time.
- [ ] Unfilled placeholders warn before sending, matching email.
- [ ] Only the rep's own workspace templates are offered.
- [ ] The picker is absent on sample contacts, where texting is unavailable, and where the contact has opted out.
- [ ] Empty, no-results, loading and error states all render.
- [ ] Browser QA covers insert, edit, send now, send later, replacement confirmation and every state above.
- [ ] Activation events are verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

* Templates written over several lines going into a message box that holds one. That box drops line breaks and puts nothing in their place, so a two-line template currently arrives with the last word of one line joined to the first word of the next. Recommended default: put a space where each line break was when a template is inserted, and only move to a taller box if reps ask for one.
* The text composer during and immediately after a call, which the parent ticket asks for. Recommended default: treat the contact's Calls and Texts composer as that composer, because it is the only one that exists, and confirm the post-call panel does not sit on top of it.

## Expected outcome

A rep can reuse an approved message from the box where they already write texts, edit it, and send it now or schedule it for later, without leaving the contact record.

## Implementation context

* Both ways of sending already share one draft and one pending state in the contact composer, so inserting into that shared draft gives Send now and Send later template support at the same time. Send one text later established that shape.
* The placeholder warning already exists for email and warns without substituting. Reuse it rather than building anything that resolves placeholders.
* The message box is currently a single line where Enter sends, and its behavior is pinned by existing tests. Any change there has to keep those passing.
* Wider background for this work is in the AI context.md on the parent ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Email Templates for Email Composer
relatedSnapshot.description:
Allow users to create, save, and reuse email templates within the email composer to reduce repetitive typing and make.

### Value to User:

* Efficiency for manual email composition
* Reduces errors and ensures correct messaging and links are used
* Adds more utility to the CRM, bringing it in line with other CRMs

### User Interface:

* **Email Composer Dropdown** - Add a searchable dropdown (combobox) where users select from their templates
  * Typing filters the list in real time
  * Templates ranked by last-used ("Recent") for that user

 <image> 

* **Email Composer Button** - Add a button near the Send & Cancel buttons called "Save as template"
* **Workspace Settings** - In Settings, add a new "CRM" option under Workspace
  * Add an "Email Template Management" section
  * Users can edit, rename, delete their templates in this section

### Requirements:

* User selects preferred template, and the saved template updates the subject and body of the email
* Supports {{variables}} in the subject and body
* User can still manually edit the text after a template is inserted
* Template selection does not auto-send nor overwrite attachments, recipients, etc.
* Selecting a new template replaces the current subject and body

---

### Architectural Notes:

* The Email Composer should be a similar/unified experience across the application.
* Whether the user sends an email from the AI SDR or the CRM, the composer UI and functionality should behave consistently.
* Treat the Email Composer as a single reusable feature to avoid maintaining multiple versions and reduce development effort.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add reusable SMS templates to every CRM text composer
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let CRM users create, save and reuse text-message templates so they can send consistent SMS without retyping the same message. Templates must be available anywhere a rep writes a CRM text, including during or immediately after a call.

## Problem

CRM has reusable email templates but no SMS equivalent. Reps have to retype common text messages, and they cannot start a scheduled text from a saved template.

## Proposed fix

Use the existing email-template experience as the model for plain-text SMS templates. Add template management plus a searchable picker that inserts a saved message into every CRM text composer while keeping the message editable before it is sent or scheduled.

## What's included

* Create, rename, edit and delete SMS templates through the same CRM settings area and permission model used for email templates.
* Search and select a template from the normal contact Calls & Texts composer.
* Use templates in the text composer shown during or immediately after a call.
* Use a selected template with either Send now or Send later once text scheduling is available.
* Match the existing email-template behavior for supported variables and unresolved-variable warnings.
* Keep this as a standalone follow-up PR. It is not part of the current text-scheduling PR stack.

Not included: changing SMS delivery, scheduling, consent, sender selection, automation, sequences or MMS.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace: somewhere to keep a text-message template, and the rules for reading and writing one.

### Wave 2: starts when priority 1 completes

Parallel: Create and manage SMS templates in settings and Insert a saved SMS template into the contact text composer. Neither depends on the other and they touch different files, so they can be built by different people and merged in either order. With capacity for only one, start the lower-numbered one first.

2. Create and manage SMS templates in settings: a place to write and look after templates. Blocked by Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace.
3. Insert a saved SMS template into the contact text composer: a picker beside the message box on the contact record. Blocked by Save reusable SMS templates in the workspace.

Cross-wave overlap: None. Nothing can start before priority 1, because both remaining tickets read the saved template and the rules it creates.

## How it should work

* Selecting a template fills the text body but never sends or schedules it automatically.
* The rep can edit the inserted text before sending.
* Choosing another template replaces the current text only after the user confirms when unsaved text would be lost.
* Template availability and sharing follow the existing email-template rules.
* The same saved templates and picker behavior are used across all CRM SMS composer surfaces.
* Existing sender, permission, consent and scheduling checks continue to apply at send time.

## Who can do what

Users can view and use the SMS templates available to them under the existing email-template access model. Creation, editing, deletion and sharing must use the same workspace boundaries and permissions as email templates.

## What the user sees

A searchable template picker beside the SMS composer, an editable inserted message, clear empty and no-results states, and the same template options in the normal contact composer and the during/post-call text composer.

## Done when

- [ ] A user can create, rename, edit and delete an SMS template.
- [ ] A user can search for and insert an available template in the contact Calls & Texts composer.
- [ ] The same template picker works in the text composer shown during or immediately after a call.
- [ ] A selected template can be edited and then sent now or scheduled for later.
- [ ] Replacing non-empty draft text requires confirmation.
- [ ] Template access stays within the correct workspace and matches email-template permissions.
- [ ] Browser QA covers management, both composer surfaces, empty/error states and Send now/Send later.
- [ ] Activation tracking is implemented through the repository tracking skill and verified in PostHog.

## Open questions

None: use the existing email-template behavior as the default wherever this ticket does not specify an SMS-only difference.

## Expected outcome

Reps can quickly reuse approved text messages from any CRM texting flow, including call follow-up, without delaying the current text-scheduling release.

## Implementation context

* AI context.md
*

relatedSnapshot.title: Send and receive Twilio attachments in CRM
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Overview.** Reps can attach files when texting from a contact or replying in Conversations, and can see and download files customers send back. The same files are available on the record without relying on Twilio download links.

**Problem and why.** Existing text inputs do not expose attachments, picture-only replies fail validation, and text rendering shows an empty-message fallback. Reps cannot complete a file exchange inside CRM.

**User experience.** A paperclip adds files with thumbnails or filename cards, upload progress and Remove. Text is optional when files are ready. Existing scheduling preserves the files. Received attachments appear in the thread and Files with their original message link and permissions.

**What's included.** Twilio's accepted MMS formats and at most 10 files, complete payload under 5 MB for JPEG/PNG/GIF-only media, and 600 KB aggregate if another supported format is present; contact and Conversations SMS; durable inbound copies; thread/activity/snippet rendering; existing scheduled sends; reuse of ticket 1’s private attachment storage/download/Files contract; funding integration. No Sendblue attachment work, template attachments, workflow attachment editor or automatic file conversion.

**Blocked by.** ENG-13825 shared attachment delivery; ENG-12611. Required UI drawing dependency on ENG-13792; its existing drawing list does not yet include messaging.

**Who can do what.** Existing authorized senders can send; only readers of the message can preview/download/list its files. Uploaded files belong to the workspace and cannot be attached through a guessed object ID or another user's unshared draft. Changing the selected line does not bypass permission, consent or funding checks.

**Done when.**

* Image-only, file-only and text-plus-files work in both SMS composers with supported Twilio senders; invalid type/count/bytes are refused before funding/dispatch.
* Read back the active Twilio webhook configuration at implementation/QA time. Cover or explicitly exclude still-configured legacy routes before claiming complete inbound coverage.
* Inbound multi-attachment SMS is copied once under the correct workspace; copy failure remains visible and retry does not duplicate the message, notification or cost.
* Scheduled attachment bytes survive long waits and retries; cancellation and revoked permission prevent dispatch; missing files never result in a partial send.
* Files/thread/activity views use one protected object and truthful attachment-only snippets. Restricted users cannot bypass permissions through downloads, bulk actions or generic signing.
* Funding, repeated operation, provider-accepted/local-write-failure and unknown-outcome cases preserve single-send/single-reservation behavior.
* Required browser and provider-boundary tests below pass; approved runtime QA uses controlled recipients. Activation events are verified landing through the existing tracking instrumentation skill.

**Reference.** Close MMS, Twilio accepted MIME types.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the reviewed surface behavior, storage and retention rules, provider limits, source anchors and validation requirements.

relatedSnapshot.title: Personalize emails and texts with reliable merge variables
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps insert person, company, owner, sender and custom-field values into reusable messages, preview the actual message for a person, and supply fallback text where needed. The same rules apply to email and SMS.

## User experience

Both template editors and all CRM email/text composer entry points offer a labelled variable picker and per-variable fallback editor. Namespaced tokens remain copyable. Preview shows the selected person, sender and company context; SMS shows the rendered length and segments. Missing values without defaults block sending and explain how to fix them.

## What's included

* `contact.name`, `contact.first_name`, `contact.last_name`, `company.name`, `contact.primary_email`, `contact.primary_phone`, `owner.name`, `sender.name`, and person/company custom fields referenced by stable definition IDs.
* Syntax such as `{{contact.first_name | default: "there"}}`; an intentionally empty fallback is allowed. Preserve valid false/zero custom values and render selected-option labels rather than IDs.
* Email subject/body and SMS body support, selected-person preview, send/schedule validation and safe HTML/text escaping. No full Liquid language, arbitrary expressions, URL/attribute interpolation or AI-generated variables.
* A saved-template selector in Conversations SMS replies, which current main lacks, plus the existing contact/call/deal/draft entry points that reuse shared composers.
* Explicit legacy-literal versus merge-format compatibility; old templates and already-scheduled messages never silently gain new evaluation behaviour.
* Team-template mode for email and SMS workflow steps, retaining existing raw-text mode.

## Blocked by

Store and preserve separate first and last names and Keep personal templates and share them with the team. The Sales Team backfill is not a blocker. UI designs are in progress and will be attached later.

## How it should work

Use the sole linked company automatically. For several companies, manual preview/composition requires a permitted linked company selection or defaults. Workflow company variables require an explicit linked company reference when ambiguous. No arbitrary first-company choice or new primary-company field.

Manual Send/Schedule blocks for missing variables without defaults and for malformed/unknown tokens. A workflow stops before dispatch with an actionable error; correction can be retried. Preview authorization respects the selected person, company, field and sender. Saved templates retain tokens, not the selected person's resolved data.

Scheduled one-off messages store the exact reviewed rendered subject/body. Workflows resolve when a send step first executes, persist one rendered claim under workspace/execution/step occurrence, and reuse it for retries. Bind stable email/SMS send identities to the claim and reconcile uncertain results before resend. Template changes cannot create a new body under an already claimed operation. Existing consent and sender/record access checks still run before dispatch.

## Done when

- [ ] Every catalogue variable and default behaves identically in both editors, preview and the relevant send/schedule paths.
- [ ] Person/sender/company switching invalidates stale preview while preserving manual edits; unauthorized IDs never expose values.
- [ ] Unknown/deleted fields, missing values, false/zero, multi-company ambiguity, unicode, HTML-like values and rendered SMS limits are covered by tests.
- [ ] Both email and SMS template workflow modes reject personal/cross-workspace/deleted templates and preserve the resolved message and send identity on retries.
- [ ] Scheduled content remains unchanged after contact/template edits, and sent history remains immutable.
- [ ] Missing-value failures are recoverable without advancing the workflow or creating a provider request.
- [ ] Browser QA covers settings, email new/reply/draft entry points, contact SMS, Conversations SMS reply, defaults, preview and scheduling; verified activation tracking is present. UI designs will be attached when James completes them.

## References

Combine Close's namespaced tags and defaults, Name 2's attribute chips, fallbacks and recipient preview, and Name 3's linked-record tokens. Team-only workflows follow Close's explicit workflow rule; do not claim Attio/Octolane document the same private-template restriction.

Preserve the protection delivered by safe email template previews. Attachments and signatures remain in their separate messaging scopes.

## Delivery order and design status

Pickup rank 3; earliest dependency wave 2. Starts after names and personal/team templates. May overlap the Sales Team backfill.

James is designing the UI. Create and plan this ticket now; attach the matching designs later. Backend/data work can proceed. Final visible controls must follow the completed designs before UI sign-off. CRM redesign handover.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the full variable catalogue, grammar, rendering, permission, scheduled-message and workflow retry contracts.

relatedSnapshot.title: Attachments in CRM
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can send and receive pictures and files in CRM texts and connected Gmail/Outlook email, and find those attachments again on the record.

## Problem and why

Current CRM composers and persistence do not complete a dependable attachment journey. Provider links alone are not durable CRM history. This master replaces local H20/H21 planning scope and supports Close migration for every workspace.

## What's included

* Received Gmail/Outlook file attachments, shared private storage, protected downloads and record Files.
* Twilio MMS attachments in contact texts, Conversations replies, message history and existing scheduled sends.
* Gmail/Outlook attachments in new mail, replies, saved drafts and scheduled messages.

## Execution order

1. ENG-13825: Keep received email attachments on CRM records establishes shared private storage, protected readback and Files.
2. ENG-13826: Send and receive Twilio attachments in CRM reuses that contract; also waits for ENG-12611 funding and its drawings.
3. ENG-13827: Send email attachments now or later from CRM reuses that contract; also waits for ENG-12569 safe sending and its drawings.

After delivery 1, deliveries 2 and 3 become eligible independently when their own blockers are satisfied. Prefer pickup 2 first; extra capacity can take 3. Provider-specific work may overlap; serialize edits to shared schema, Files and attachment components. There is no Twilio-to-email blocker. All three require their attachment drawings under ENG-13792 for visible release.

## Agreed behavior

Accept all Twilio-supported MMS formats, with at most 10 files: the complete payload must be under 5 MB for JPEG/PNG/GIF-only media, or within 600 KB aggregate when another supported type is present. Outbound email permits 20 MB raw attachments total, also respecting encoded-message and verified lower mailbox limits. No attachment templates, Sendblue attachment work, conversion, bulk sending or new texting providers.

Copy inbound ordinary file bytes into private CRM storage, including Gmail and Outlook. Copy up to 150,000,000 bytes per file and per message, at most 100 files per received message; preserve metadata and an explicit reason when not copied. Copied files survive mailbox removal and source deletion. Retain files for the message lifetime; clean uploads unreferenced for 24 hours while protecting draft, schedule and uncertain-send references.

Show non-inline sent/received files in record Files with Email/Text source and Open message. Respect original-message access plus record access; exclude inline/CID images. Reuse one stored object rather than duplicating files across records.

## Delivery requirements

Each child owns a complete usable outcome, its drawings and appropriate browser/provider verification. ENG-13792 is the design handover dependency; its existing drawing list needs these attachment states. Backend preparation can start before drawings. ENG-13342 retains ownership of the future Conversations email screen and consumes the shared attachment composer/renderer.

Twilio uses ENG-12611 funding and ENG-12603 pricing/usage contracts. Copying or downloading an attachment is not another message charge. Email delivery is independent of Twilio funding.

## Done when

All three child outcomes pass their acceptance criteria, source-message permissions cover previews/downloads/Files, schedules preserve files without duplicate sends, and required activation events are verified. No implementation or live QA is claimed by this plan. No production backfill, new fee activation or provider-media deletion is included.

relatedSnapshot.title: Send and receive email attachments in CRM Conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can attach files to emails they send from Conversations, now or scheduled, through their connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox. Files that people send them arrive with the email in the CRM and can be downloaded from the thread and the person's Files tab. This ticket now also covers received files, which were planned on ENG-13825 but never built.

## Problem

* **Sending:** the email composer in Conversations has no Attach button. Gmail sends every email as one plain part, Outlook never adds files, and scheduled emails cannot hold files. Reps switch to Gmail or Outlook to send a proposal or contract.
* **Receiving:** when a lead replies with a document, the CRM stores the email text but drops the file details. Nobody can see or open the file from the CRM. None of the roughly 450,000 Gmail and Outlook emails synced in the last 14 days have any stored file.

## User experience

* **Attach:** in the Conversations email composer (docked and full editor), the rep clicks Attach or drops files onto the email. Each file shows as a card with upload progress and Remove, and the tray shows the total against 20 MB. A blocked type or a file over the limit is refused in words before upload. Send and Schedule wait until uploads finish.
* **Send now or later:** the email arrives with its files in the recipient's inbox, threaded as before. Scheduled emails keep their files until they send or are cancelled. The scheduled preview in the thread lists the files.
* **Drafts:** files stay attached if the rep switches conversations and comes back. Applying a template leaves the files alone. Files are not carried over when replying or forwarding.
* **In the thread:** file chips on sent and received emails can be downloaded. While a received file is still being saved it shows "Saving…". If saving failed, it shows the reason and a Retry button.
* **Files tab:** sent and received email files appear on the person's Files tab, read-only, alongside text files.

## What's included

* Sending from Conversations with Gmail and Outlook connected mailboxes: new email, reply and forward, now or scheduled.
* Saving received files from Gmail and Outlook into our private storage, so they stay readable if the mailbox disconnects or the original email is deleted.
* Download from the thread and Files tab, with the same access rule as reading the email itself.
* Activation tracking for attaching, sending with files and downloading.

**Not included:** inline images inside an email body (signature logos, pasted pictures) render as today and are not listed as files. Attachments on the record Emails tab (ENG-14350) are not in scope. The AI SDR inbox and campaign sending tools, and attachments inside templates, are also not in scope.

## How it should work

* **Limits:** up to 20 files and 20 MB in total per sent email. Executable and archive types are blocked (the existing CRM blocklist). Received files are saved up to 35 MB per file (covers Gmail's 25 MB and Outlook's default 35 MB limits), 150 MB per email and 100 files per email. Anything larger stays listed with "Too large to save".
* **Which received files are saved automatically:** files on newly synced emails in CRM v2 workspaces, where the email thread is linked to a person. Older history (first import of a mailbox) and emails not yet linked to a person are not copied in bulk. They show a Save button that copies the file on demand while the mailbox is connected. This keeps storage cost in line with what reps actually open.
* **Outlook items and cloud links:** an attached Outlook item or a OneDrive link is listed with "Open in Outlook" wording, not saved as a file.
* **Sending safely:** an email with files is sent once. If the provider's answer is lost, the existing "never lose a sent email" check (ENG-12569) settles it, and the rep is never offered "send again". A scheduled email whose files are missing fails with a reason and sends nothing.

## Who can do what

* Anyone who may send from a mailbox may attach files to emails from it. A file uploaded for one draft can only be used by the person who uploaded it.
* Downloading an email file needs the same access as reading that email's content in Conversations. The Files tab also requires access to the person.

## Done when

* Gmail and Outlook both deliver new, reply and forward emails with files to a real recipient mailbox, threaded correctly. Scheduled emails with files send with their files, and cancelling releases them.
* A received email with files on a linked person shows downloadable files in Conversations and on the Files tab. The copy survives a mailbox disconnect, and duplicate syncs never create duplicate files.
* Failed saves show a reason and Retry. Retrying does not create a second file.
* Someone without access to an email's content cannot list or download its files by any route.
* Attach, send-with-files and download events are verified landing in PostHog.

## Implementation context

* **Storage:** files are private `crm_file` rows under the message-attachments path, as texting files are. One small new table tracks each email file (received, sent or scheduled), its source mailbox and its save state. Rows are written in the same transaction as the email. A background job copies received files, one run per email at a time, and a sweeper re-queues anything stuck, so retries and duplicate syncs converge.
* **Immutable sent files:** when an email with files is sent or scheduled, each file is copied to a server-owned object. The bytes cannot change afterwards, and uploads stop counting against the rep's upload allowance.
* **Send once:** an email sent now with files uses the existing send-once record that scheduled emails use.
* **Off switch:** a workspace flag stops new attachment uploads, sends, schedules and copies. Already-scheduled emails still send with their files.
* **Provider work:** a tested multipart MIME builder for Gmail using the upload endpoint (threading kept). For Outlook, files are added to the existing draft before `/send`, with upload sessions for files of 3 MB or more. There is no automatic retry of the final send call.
* **Rollback** is the off switch, then fix forward. A code revert is safe only when no scheduled email with files is still waiting, because older code would send those emails without their files.
* **QA dependency:** one Gmail and one Outlook test mailbox connected on the preview workspace, sending only to our own test addresses.
* Name 4 planning context: send context, receive context. Where they conflict, this description wins (for example, inline image rendering is out and the received-file cap is 35 MB).

relatedSnapshot.title: Commerce transactional email templates
Keep received email attachments on CRM records
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Overview.** Reps can open files received through connected Gmail and Outlook accounts directly from the email or record Files tab. The stored copy remains available if the mailbox later disconnects.

**Problem and why.** Provider readers find attachment metadata but the CRM sync/persistence contract drops it. A rep can see an email while missing the document it refers to.

**User experience.** File cards appear below the message; inline images render in the body. Copy progress/failure is visible without hiding the message. Files lists non-inline attachments with an Email label and Open message action.

**What's included.** Gmail/Outlook file attachments, metadata preservation, authenticated provider fetch, idempotent private storage copies, authorized email/Files rendering and recovery. Own the shared private attachment storage, message-aware download and Files contract for all three tickets. No Company One/EmailBison support, recursive attached-email conversion, cloud-drive-link copying, historical bulk backfill or template changes.

**Blocked by.** Required received-email drawing under ENG-13792.

**Who can do what.** Copy only admitted, workspace-bound mail. Permission to view an attachment equals permission to view the original message, including through linked records. Account disconnection does not broaden visibility. Late workers must not cross mailbox-workspace rebinding.

**Done when.**

* Durable copy rows use the specified unique provider identity, lease, retry/backoff and states; worker and manual retries coalesce, with binding checks before fetch and commit.
* Gmail and Outlook file metadata reaches CRM and each ordinary file within 150,000,000 bytes per file and per message, with at most 100 files per received message is copied once; retries, duplicate sync pages and crashes do not duplicate objects/listings.
* Normal attachments and inline/CID images render correctly; inline images stay out of Files. Non-file Outlook attachments have an explicit representation rather than silently disappearing.
* A provider outage, removed source file or bounded-copy failure displays a reason and safe recovery where available; message text remains readable.
* Mailbox disconnection/source-email deletion leaves already copied files readable to still-authorized CRM users.
* Cross-workspace, restricted-reader, generic-signing and Files aggregation tests pass. No new provider import is triggered by merely listing Files.
* Activation tracking is verified landing using the repository instrumentation skill for attachment viewing/downloading; no filenames or content in events.
* Contact email surface is demonstrated; the future Conversations email surface reuses this renderer through existing ENG-13342, which remains owner of that screen.

**Reference and related work.** Close Files. Relate ENG-13342 and ENG-13799; do not wait for shared-visibility mode to implement the current permission policy.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the reviewed surface behavior, storage and retention rules, provider limits, source anchors and validation requirements.

relatedSnapshot.title: Build supplier outreach template library
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Pre-built email templates for cold outreach to potential suppliers. Provides a starting point for supplier acquisition communications, with variable substitution for personalization. Integrates with the existing cold email / AI SDR system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pre-built templates:
  - Initial contact: introduce store, express interest in carrying their products
  - Follow-up #1: reference initial email, highlight mutual benefits
  - Follow-up #2: offer specific partnership terms
  - Product inquiry: ask about specific product lines, MOQ, pricing
  - Partnership proposal: formal proposal with terms
- [ ] Template variables: `{{supplierName}}`, `{{productCategory}}`, `{{storeName}}`, `{{senderName}}`, `{{companyWebsite}}`
- [ ] Save custom templates
- [ ] Use templates from cold email tool / AI SDR when contacting suppliers
- [ ] Admin route: `/dashboard/[orgSlug]/store/supplier-templates`

## Codebase Reference

* Schema: `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts` — add `supplierEmailTemplate` table
* Cold email system: existing cold email / AI SDR tools for sending
* Admin pages: `Page`/`PageHeader`/`PageBody` layout components
* Sheet: use `Sheet` component for template create/edit form
* tRPC: `trpc/routers/commerce/` — add template CRUD procedures

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `supplierEmailTemplate` table in `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts`: id, name, subject, body (text with `{{variable}}` placeholders), isDefault (boolean — true for pre-built templates), organizationId, createdAt, updatedAt
2. Create tRPC procedures:
   * `listSupplierTemplates()`: return all templates for org (defaults + custom)
   * `getSupplierTemplate(id)`: return single template
   * `createSupplierTemplate({ name, subject, body })`: insert custom template
   * `updateSupplierTemplate(id, data)`: update template (prevent editing isDefault templates, allow duplicating them)
   * `deleteSupplierTemplate(id)`: delete custom templates only
3. Seed default templates on first access (check if defaults exist, create if not):
   * Initial Contact: subject "Partnership Opportunity — {{storeName}}", body introducing store and interest
   * Follow-up #1: subject "Following up — {{storeName}} × {{supplierName}}", body referencing initial email
   * Follow-up #2: subject "Partnership terms — {{storeName}}", body with specific terms
   * Product Inquiry: subject "Product inquiry from {{storeName}}", body asking about lines/MOQ/pricing
   * Partnership Proposal: subject "Formal partnership proposal", body with detailed terms
4. Create admin page at `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/store/supplier-templates/page.tsx`:
   * List templates with name, subject preview, isDefault badge
   * Click → Sheet with template editor (name, subject, body textarea)
   * Variable insertion toolbar: buttons to insert `{{supplierName}}`, `{{productCategory}}`, etc. at cursor position
   * "New Template" button → blank Sheet
5. Integration: when sending from CRM supplier board (P2.09), allow selecting a supplier template → auto-fill with supplier's data
6. Run `bun db:generate` after schema changes

relatedSnapshot.title: Keep personal templates and share them with the team
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can save personal email and text templates, then share useful ones with the team immediately. Admins retain oversight without an approval queue.

## User experience

Template settings and composer pickers distinguish Personal and Team. New templates default to Personal; existing templates remain Team. “Share with team” explains the visibility change and promotes the same template immediately. Personal means accessible to the creator and workspace admins, which is stated in the UI.

## What's included

* Visibility and permissions on both existing template tables, settings editors, selectors and save-as-template actions.
* Creator/admin editing rules, promotion actor/time, stale-edit protection and clear name-conflict handling.
* Separate case-insensitive active-name uniqueness for team templates and each creator's personal templates, independently per channel.
* A shared server access policy usable by the later workflow template selector; personal templates cannot be selected for automation.

## Who can do what

Members with channel access can read/use team templates; creator plus admins/owners can edit/delete them. Personal contents are inaccessible to other ordinary members across direct IDs, search, recent usage, preview, copy, bulk actions and use paths. Admin oversight never bypasses record or sender permissions. Creator deletion makes personal templates admin-only orphans, not shared content. Membership removal revokes access even if the user account remains.

## How it should work

Promotion is immediate, without approval. A team-name collision requires a different name and never overwrites another template. Editing or deleting templates cannot alter sent messages. Do not convert a team template back to personal; allow a personal copy instead.

Roll out visibility-aware readers and writers while personal creation is disabled. Enable personal creation only after old instances and routable deployments that return every workspace template are drained. Rollback must retain those privacy checks or disable template access, never expose private rows through old readers.

## Done when

- [ ] Personal/team behaviour works for both email and SMS, including saving from composers and promotion.
- [ ] Another member or workspace cannot retrieve personal contents through any endpoint or cached/recent result; creator/admin access works as described.
- [ ] Promotion, rename and bulk actions remain correct under concurrent requests, duplicate names and stale edits.
- [ ] Creator/member removal, orphan recovery and privacy-preserving rollback are tested.
- [ ] Existing templates stay team-visible; personal creation cannot precede privacy-aware deployment completion.
- [ ] Browser QA covers settings and pickers, empty/error states, member/admin views and promotion; verified activation tracking is present. UI designs will be attached when James completes them.

## References

Close supports shared templates; Name 3 documents personal and workspace templates. Name 2 makes templates workspace-editable. Acquisity keeps the requested personal option with deliberate sharing and admin oversight; mandatory promotion approval is explicitly excluded.

Relate to the completed email templates and SMS templates deliveries.

## Delivery order and design status

Pickup rank 2; earliest dependency wave 1. No feature-ticket blocker. Functionally independent from names, but reconcile shared CRM schema/migration work before concurrent changes. May overlap Sales Team backfill once names is deployed.

James is designing the UI. Create and plan this ticket now; attach the matching designs later. Backend/data work can proceed. Final visible controls must follow the completed designs before UI sign-off. CRM redesign handover.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains the permission model, two-stage privacy rollout, schema details and required verification.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add Variable Validation, Autocomplete, and Safety Checks for Email Templates
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue Identified:

Currently, variables in the Cold Email Agent (e.g., `{{firstName}}`, `{{companyName}}`) must be typed manually. There’s no way to select variables from available lead fields or confirm that each one is valid.

**This makes it easy for users to:**

* Mistype variable names (e.g., `{{fristname}}` instead of `{{firstName}}`)
* Forget to close brackets (e.g., `{{firstName}`)
* Use variables that don’t exist or aren’t populated for certain leads

As a result, campaigns could accidentally be sent out with broken or empty placeholders.

## Solutions:

* Provide an autocomplete or dropdown list of valid variables user can select when editing variants
* Validate all variables in a template before allowing it to be saved
* Warn or block saving if there’s a `{{` without a closing `}}`
* Provide fallback options if a lead does not contain the variable information
  * E.g., "Hi {{firstName}}," --> {{Hi there,}}

Autocomplete/dropdown example from Company One:

 <image> 

## Impact:

* Prevents mass sends with broken personalization
* Improves user confidence in variant setup
* Reduces QA/Support workload from user-side variant errors

## Acceptance Criteria:

- [ ] User can select valid variables from a dropdown or autocomplete when editing
- [ ] System validates all variables and blocks saving on errors
- [ ] Fallback text displays correctly when data is missing

---

## Additional Improvement for Variables:

In the variant preview modal, show the information from one of their leads (possibly from a dropdown) instead of making the user manually type in fake data to see how variables will fill in.

* This will help validate that their email variant will work with the information contained in their lead list.
* Makes it easier for the user too. Instead of the user having to manually type "Name 11" into the First Name field in the Variant Preview modal, maybe we should show them information from one of their leads.
